parts.name: Septal cartilage
parts.attachment_or_location: quadrangular plate completing the nasal septum in front of the vomer and the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid
parts.function_note: The commonest site of septal deviation, and the usual donor for grafting in rhinoplasty. Kiesselbach's plexus lies on its anterior surface, the source of most anterior epistaxis.
parts.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

parts.name: Lateral (upper lateral) nasal cartilages
parts.attachment_or_location: triangular plates continuous with the septal cartilage, forming the middle nasal vault
parts.function_note: Their junction with the septum forms the internal nasal valve, the narrowest part of the whole airway and the principal site of nasal airflow resistance.
parts.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

parts.name: Major and minor alar cartilages
parts.attachment_or_location: U-shaped cartilages forming the nostril rims and the nasal tip
parts.function_note: Support the external nasal valve; their collapse on brisk inspiration is what a nasal dilator strip counteracts.
parts.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

function: Give the lower two-thirds of the nose its shape and keep the nasal airway patent. Being cartilage rather than bone, this part of the nose deforms rather than fractures.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

parts.name: Auricular cartilage
parts.attachment_or_location: single elastic plate shaped into the helix, antihelix, tragus, antitragus and concha; continuous with the cartilage of the external acoustic meatus
parts.function_note: Elastic cartilage with tightly adherent perichondrium and no subcutaneous layer over its lateral surface -- which is why a haematoma that strips the perichondrium starves the cartilage and produces cauliflower ear unless drained.
parts.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

parts.name: Cartilage of the external acoustic meatus
parts.attachment_or_location: forms the outer third of the canal; the inner two-thirds are bony
parts.function_note: The cartilaginous outer third is mobile, which is why pulling the auricle up and back straightens the canal for otoscopy.
parts.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

function: Shapes the auricle for sound collection and localisation, and keeps the outer external acoustic meatus patent while allowing it to deform.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
